title: beth-mathematician answer
description: The typed answer. Passed to Claude Code with --json-schema and validated again by the launcher; the grader reads result_expr, and scripts/agentkit/render_derivation.py writes derivation.md from the rest.

result_expr.description: The result as one SymPy expression, using only the work order's allowed names. Empty when blocked.

title.description: A few words: what this step produces.

why.description: One to three plain sentences: what this step does, and why it is the next step. Symbols in LaTeX between $...$, never Unicode or ASCII names.

from.description: IDs of earlier steps, 'given', or assumption numbers A1, A2, ... (1-based, in the order of assumptions_used).

operation.description: The named operation: multiply by w, integrate over (0, L), integration by parts, substitution of S3, ...

latex.description: The step's one displayed equation in LaTeX, without $ delimiters. Every symbol in it is in the work order or in your symbols list.

function.description: The function in scratch/check.py that checks this step, or empty when the step has no check.

printed.description: What the check printed; or, with no function, why the step cannot be checked by a tool.

steps.description: The derivation as a linear story: each step follows from the given equations, the assumptions or earlier steps by one named operation. derivation.md is generated from these fields.

symbols.description: Every symbol you introduced that the work order does not define: parameters, material properties, functions. A quantity that depends on others is a function; write its name with its arguments, for example k(phi, T). Units in SI, written like 'W m^-1 K^-1'; '1' for dimensionless. Declare every symbol your step equations use that the work order does not define, including intermediate ones (a residual R, a curvature K, a profile phi_0).

latex.description: How the symbol is written in LaTeX, for example \rho_{vs}(T) or M(\phi, T); the same string you use in the step equations.

typical.description: A typical value in the stated SI units for ice and vapor near 200 K, to the right order of magnitude (for a function, a typical value of the function).

assumptions_used.description: Numbered A1, A2, ... in this order; write symbols in LaTeX between $...$.

neglected.description: Every physical effect you considered and left out, with the reason it is small (an estimate where you can give one).

questions.description: What stopped the work, or what the user should decide. Empty when done.

result_latex.description: The result as one LaTeX equation (no $ delimiters), for example R = \partial_t\phi + ... = 0. Empty when blocked.
